**Tier 2** — canonical — the only tier humans edit · owned by `data-ingestion` · `public.inbound_logistics`

**One row is** One supply arc as the user uploaded it: this supplier can deliver this material to this plant, at this price and lead time, in this volume. NOT deduplicated — a second upload of the same row makes a second row (D5).

### `lead_time`

How long this supplier takes to deliver this material. The contract fixes the unit at WEEKS; `time_unit` does not apply to it and never has.

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | `numeric` |
| Grain | `level` |
| Unit | `weeks` — column, named by `lead_time_unit` |
| Added by | `20250820145837_5a2d95f1-7a5f-4bbb-8ac8-995d53011bce.sql` |
| Read by the engine | `project_map.py::_map_supply -> SupplierLink.lead_time_weeks` |
| Transform | _duration_to_weeks(lead_time, lead_time_unit), then round and clamp to [1, 51] |
| When NULL, the engine uses | 2 weeks, with a `warn` MappingWarning |
| Validated at ingest | numeric > 0 |
| Rendered at | *not yet recorded (WP 5.1)* |

**The engine calls this `recommended`.** Supplier lead time per sourcing arc — missing values default to 2 weeks.

Fallback chain, from the engine's own registry: constant 2 (warn).

**Substitutions** — every point where a value you did not supply can stand in
for one you did.

| When | The value used | Shown as | Visible where |
|---|---|---|---|
| the column is NULL or zero | 2 weeks | `default` | MappingWarning on the run's mapping report |

**Resolution** — how a value is decided when more than one source could supply one.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default mode | `asserted` |
| Assertable by | `csv_upload` |
| Estimable from | `observations.receipts (Phase 7+)` |
| Hybrid (centre / spread) | `inbound_logistics.lead_time` / `materials.lead_time_dist + materials.lead_time_cv` |
| On conflict | `assertion_wins` |

The engine already supports this split and has since scsim was written: SupplierLink carries lead_time_weeks (the CENTRE) separately from lead_time_dist and lead_time_cv (the SPREAD), and core/engine.py samples only when the distribution is not DETERMINISTIC and the CV is above zero. So deterministic is not a degenerate case bolted on — it is the default path, and it skips sampling entirely. default_mode is `asserted` for the same reason: the user states the lead time, and the spread is opt-in. estimable_from names the observations tier that does not exist yet (tier 2-O, reserved in WP 1.2) rather than leaving the door open to estimating this from whatever happens to be lying around.

> Was `unit_source: fixed` until WP 1.3, and fixed by OMISSION rather than by contract: the engine read a `lead_time_unit` that no column supplied, so every lead time was taken as weeks whatever the user meant. The column now exists and `unit` stays `weeks` because that is what NULL still means.

What one unit of this material costs from this supplier, delivered.

| | |
|---|---|

**The engine calls this `recommended`.** Purchase cost per sourcing arc — a missing price defaults to 1.0 and distorts procurement spend.

Fallback chain, from the engine's own registry: constant 1 (warn).

**Substitutions** — every point where a value you did not supply can stand in
for one you did.

| When | The value used | Shown as | Visible where |
|---|---|---|---|
| NULL, zero or negative | 1.0 | `default` | MappingWarning on the run's mapping report |
| `materials.cost` is unset for this material | this arc's price becomes the material's cost, via the cheapest inbound arc | `derived` | the effective-economics badge in /policies |

**Resolution** — how a value is decided when more than one source could supply one.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default mode | `asserted` |
| Assertable by | `csv_upload` |
| Estimable from | **never** — this value may not be estimated |
| Hybrid (centre / spread) | **none** — the engine has no variability field for this quantity |
| On conflict | `assertion_wins` |

hybrid is NULL because scsim has nowhere to put a spread: cost and unit_price are bare floats on Material and Product, with no distribution, no CV and no sampling path anywhere in the engine. Recording `hybrid: null` here is a statement about the ENGINE, not about the world — prices obviously vary. Giving them a spread is an engine change on the scsim track; see the RFC in PLAN.md §14. Do not invent one in this contract: a contract that describes a capability the engine does not have is how a fallback ends up in code with no contract entry, which is what I6 forbids in the other direction.

> The user types `unit_price` and the engine calls it `cost`. Both names are recorded because the manual must lead with the one the user typed (D21).

A unit is never estimated. NULL means weeks, matching project_map.py::_duration_to_weeks, and the column's CHECK constraint only admits units public.unit_days() knows.

> Added by WP 1.3 (D9). The engine had read this field since the scsim bridge was written; no column supplied it, so `r.get("lead_time_unit")` returned None on every row and a lead time entered in days was read as weeks — seven times too long, with no warning, because nothing in the chain knew a unit was expected. This is also the first use of the `contract` provenance state reserved in WP 1.2: the weeks default is supplied by this document, not guessed by code.
